# Overview {#overview}

This architecture centers on an event-driven bridge between the Web App and a Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) Wrapper. The **Web Processor** (in the WebView) serializes and validates messages, forwarding events both ways so web and native stay in sync; it also dispatches **Web Processor Events** back into the site when native needs web-side action. Inside KMP, a shared **Event Bus** coordinates cross-manager orchestration: **Manager Subscribers** listen for **Manager Events** (and Web signals), do light shaping/guarding, and call **Manager Handlers**. Handlers contain platform-specific effects, SDK calls, UI updates, network, then return results or follow-ups to close the loop. On iOS, **NotificationCenter** serves as the native bridge when KMP can’t interoperate directly: the KMP layer emits **Kotlin Processor Events**, **Native Subscribers** receive them with minimal logic, and **Native Handlers** execute iOS native-level work. The guiding principles are: keep routing thin and testable in subscribers, isolate effects in handlers, prefer Kotlin implementations where possible, and use NotificationCenter only when native APIs are required.

![][image1]

# Web Processor {#web-processor}

The Web Processor is a script attached to the WebView that bridges the loaded Web App and the Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) Wrapper. It serializes messages, validates payloads, and forwards events in both directions so native managers and the Web surface stay synchronized.

# Event Bus {#event-bus}

The Event Bus is the KMP app’s internal messaging layer. Managers (and the Web Processor) emit events that Subscribers consume; Subscribers apply light shaping and invoke Handlers to execute the action. All cross-manager orchestration flows through this bus to keep routing consistent and testable.

# iOS Notification Center {#ios-notification-center}

On iOS, NotificationCenter acts as the bridge from KMP to native Swift. The KMP layer emits notifications with data when platform APIs are required; lightweight Native Subscribers receive them and delegate to Native Handlers. When needed, NotificationCenter can also publish back into the KMP Event Bus to complete the loop.

# Web Processor Subscribers {#web-processor-subscribers}

**Web Processor Subscribers** listen on the Web Bridge for events emitted by the Web App. When a matching event arrives, a subscriber validates and shapes the payload, applies any required logic, and emits the corresponding Manager event to drive native behavior.

# Web Processor Events {#web-processor-events}

**Web Processor Events** are outbound dispatches from the Wrapper to the loaded website via the Web Bridge. They’re used when the native layer needs to trigger an in-web action or communicate data back to the WebView, keeping state synchronized in both directions.

# Manager Subscribers {#manager-subscribers}

**Manager Handlers** listen for internal **Manager Events** (and relevant Web Processor signals), validate and shape the payload, then emit the appropriate call into the manager’s platform layer using delegates. They centralize orchestration, deciding *what* should happen and *when*, while keeping platform-specific details out of routing logic.

## Manager Events {#manager-events}

**Manager Events** are internal signals produced by other managers or by the Web Processor. Subscribers consume these events and invoke the appropriate platform handlers to execute the call to action or make decisions, cleanly separating event routing from platform-specific implementation.

## Manager Handlers {#manager-handlers}

**Manager Handlers** are the platform-specific implementations that execute the requested action on iOS/Android (and any shared KMP logic). They perform the side effects, network calls, SDK invocations, UI updates, and return results or follow-up signals back to Subscribers (and, when needed, to the Web Processor) to complete the loop.

## Manager Delegates {#manager-delegates}

# Kotlin Processor Events {#kotlin-processor-events}

**Kotlin Processor Events** are iOS-only signals emitted from the KMP layer to request Swift-side execution when direct interoperability isn’t practical. Use them sparingly, prefer Kotlin-native implementations whenever possible. Events are carried via NotificationCenter (an event bus mirroring KMP’s) with simple, serializable payloads, and are consumed by Native Subscribers that delegate to Native Handlers.

# Native Subscribers {#native-subscribers}

**Native Subscribers** are Lightweight NotificationCenter observers that listen for Kotlin Processor Events from the KMP app, perform minimal validation/guard checks, and immediately delegate to the appropriate Native Handler. They avoid business logic and heavy shaping to keep routing predictable and testable.

# Native Handlers {#native-handlers}

**Native Handlers** are iOS-level implementations that execute the requested action using native SDKs/APIs when Kotlin cannot. They handle side effects (UI updates on the main thread, network/SDK calls), enforce error handling and idempotency, attach analytics/breadcrumbs as needed, and return results via callbacks or follow-up events back to KMP.
